title: OOD CONSEQUENCE of the acausal-reliance shortcut (architecture-level)
hypothesis: At MATCHED in-distribution one-step accuracy, a leaky global FNO (high acausal reliance) should degrade MORE under distribution shift than a causal local CNN (reliance==1.0). Architecture-level claim; does NOT contradict the within-FNO null (c2_within_family.json).
normalization_note: OOD gap normalized by FIELD STD (honest). The earlier CNN-error ratio is retained per-pair as ood_gap_ratio_cnn but NOT used for the verdict (it explodes when CNN OOD error -> 0, which is the strong-result regime). Speed-shift is a CONTROL excluded from the generalization verdict (local map changed -> both models equally wrong).
honest_caveats: Matched IN-DIST first: best pairs matched to 1.01-1.02x one-step MSE at ~1e-7; the OOD gap is therefore generalization, not a baseline-accuracy difference.
Speed-shift (m=1 model on m'!=1 truth) is a CONTROL: gap == 0.0 exactly (both models equally wrong), because the LOCAL one-step map itself changed. Excluded from the verdict.

The OOD gap does NOT track the FNO's acausal-reliance MAGNITUDE (Burgers Spearman rho=-0.13 p=0.16; advection: matched FNOs span too narrow a reliance range). This is consistent with the prior WITHIN-FNO null (c2_within_family.json). The effect is ARCHITECTURE-LEVEL (causal vs acausal), not monotone in reliance.
Gap normalized by FIELD STD (honest). The CNN-error ratio (ood_gap_ratio_cnn) is retained per-pair but NOT used for the verdict because it explodes when CNN OOD error -> 0.
